newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen softer at open, awaits GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen softer at open, awaits GDP data.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open slightly softer on Thursday, taking early cues from a stream of economic data but vulnerable to some profit-taking after their recent run-up.

Stocks, which soared to fresh records on Wednesday as bond yields slid, would today face data on second quarter gross domestic product, weekly jobless claims and the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index for July.
The number of Americans making first-time claims for jobless benefits fell last week to the lowest level in more than 23 years, the government reported.
Weekly jobless claims fell to 277,000 in the week ended July 26 from 299,000 the week before. That undershot Wall Street economists' consensus forecast of 306,000.
